children.translated_text: All this is merely cognition (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), because of the appearance of non-existent objects,
just as one with an eye-disease (<s>taimirika</s>) sees non-existent hairs, floaters, and the like. (1)
[Objection:] The restriction of place and time, the non-restriction to a [particular] mental continuum (<s>santāna</s>),

children.text: na ca kṛtyakriyā yuktā vijñaptiryadi nārthataḥ // Vvṛ_2 //
children.translated_text: and the efficacy of action (<s>kṛtyakriyā</s>) would not be tenable if cognition were not from [external] objects. (2)
[Reply:] The restriction of place and so forth is established, as in a dream; and as for the non-restriction to a [particular] continuum, as with <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) —
for all [of them share] the seeing of the river of pus and the like. (3)
Efficacy of action [is established] as in the case of injury in a dream; and as in hell —
for all the seeing of hell-guardians and the like, and the injury by them [occurs without real external objects]. (4)

children.text: tiraścāṃ sambhavaḥ svarge yathā ca narake tathā /
children.translated_text: Just as animals are born in the heavens, so too in the hells [the guardians are not actual hell-beings];

children.text: na pretānāṃ yatastajjaṃ duḥkhaṃ nānubhavanti te // Vvṛ_5 //
children.translated_text: and [the river of pus is] not produced by the <s>pretas</s>, because they do not experience the suffering born from that. (5)

children.text: iṣyate pariṇāmaśca kiṃ vijñānasya neṣyate // Vvṛ_6 //
children.translated_text: and also their transformation — why is [the same] not accepted for consciousness? (6)

body.translated_text: If it is accepted that real beings are born there by those <s>karmas</s>,

children.translated_text: The <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of <s>karma</s> is in one [place], and the fruit is imagined in another;

children.text: tatraiva neṣyate yatra vāsanā kiṃ nu kāraṇaṃ // Vvṛ_7 //
children.translated_text: why is [the fruit] not accepted right there where the <s>vāsanā</s> resides — what is the reason? (7)
The existence of <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) such as <s>rūpa</s> (form) and the rest was stated
by [the <s>Buddha</s>] with a special intention, for the sake of those who are to be guided [by that teaching], just as [he spoke of] spontaneously-born beings (<s>upapāduka</s>). (8)

children.text: nāstīha satva ātmā vā dharmāstvete sahetukāḥ
children.translated_text: 'There is no being (<s>sattva</s>) here, nor self (<s>ātman</s>); but these <s>dharmas</s> exist with causes.'
Since cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>) arises from its own seed, having whatever appearance it manifests,
the Sage (<s>Muni</s>) taught those [causes] as two kinds of <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base). (9)
Thus, that [teaching of external sense-bases] is an entry into the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>); but otherwise,
the [other] teaching is an entry into the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), by means of the [conceptually] constructed self. (10)

children.text: na tadekaṃ na cānekaṃ viṣayaḥ paramāṇuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The object is neither one nor many when analyzed in terms of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>);

children.text: na ca te saṃhatā yasmātparamāṇurna sidhyati // Vvṛ_11 //
children.translated_text: and they are not combined [into aggregates], since the atom is not established. (11)
By the simultaneous conjunction of six [atoms], the atom would have six parts;
if the six [atoms] occupied the same location, the aggregate would be merely atom-sized. (12)
If atoms have no conjunction, of what then is the conjunction of their aggregates?

children.text: na cānavayavatvena tatsaṃyogād na sidhyati // Vvṛ_13 //
children.translated_text: And [the atom's] conjunction is not established because of its having no parts (<s>anavayavatva</s>). (13)
That which has directional parts — its unity is not tenable;

children.text: chāyāvṛtī kathaṃ vā anyo na piṇḍaścenna tasya te // Vvṛ_14 //
children.translated_text: or how [could there be] shadow and obstruction? If there is no aggregate, then those [properties] do not belong to it. (14)
If [the object were] one, there would be no progressive movement; there would be no simultaneous grasping and non-grasping;

children.text: vicchinnānekavṛttiśca sūkṣmānīkṣā ca no bhavet // Vvṛ_15 //
children.translated_text: there would be no separate, multiple states; and there would be no perception of subtle [things]. (15)

children.text: pratyakṣabuddhiḥ svapnādau yathā sa ca yadā tadā /
children.translated_text: Direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), as in a dream and so forth — when that [cognition occurs], at that time,

children.text: na so 'rtho dṛśyate tasya pratyakṣatvaṃ kathaṃ mataṃ // Vvṛ_16 //
children.translated_text: that object is not seen; so how is its directness (<s>pratyakṣatva</s>) maintained? (16)

children.text: uktaṃ yathā tadābhāsā vijñaptiḥ smaraṇaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: As stated, cognition having that appearance [arises], and memory [arises] from that;
one who has not yet awakened does not apprehend the non-existence of the objects in the dream-vision. (17)
Through mutual dominant condition (<s>adhipati</s>), cognitions are mutually regulated;

children.text: middhenopahataṃ cittaṃ svapne tenāsamaṃ phalaṃ // Vvṛ_18 //
children.translated_text: consciousness impaired by torpor (<s>middha</s>) produces a dream, therefore the fruit [in dreams] is not equal [to that in waking]. (18)
Death [results] from a special transformation in another's cognition, as [there is] harm [from others' thoughts];
memory-loss and the like of some [beings arise] from the mental power of <s>piśācas</s> (spirits) and the like. (19)
And how, then, [is explained] the emptying of the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest through the anger of the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages)?

children.text: manodaṇḍo mahāvadyaḥ kathaṃ vā tena sidhyati // Vvṛ_20 //
children.translated_text: And how is [it proved that] the mental act (<s>manodaṇḍa</s>) is of great culpability? (20)
one's own knowledge of mind [is inaccurate] due to ignorance — just so, the domain of a <s>Buddha</s> [is beyond]. (21)

body.translated_text: How is the knowledge of those who read others' minds inaccurate? Just as

children.translated_text: This establishment of consciousness-only (<s>vijñaptimātratāsiddhi</s>) has been accomplished by me

children.text: kṛteyaṃ sarvathā sā tu na cintyā buddhagocaraḥ // Vvṛ_22 //
children.translated_text: according to my own capacity; but in its entirety, it is the inconceivable domain of a <s>Buddha</s>. (22)

body.translated_text: The <s>Viṃśatikā</s> (Twenty Verses), the Establishment of Consciousness-Only (<s>Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi</s>). This is the work of master <s>Vasubandhu</s>.
